today_summary: GCM26 marked $3,969.5, recovering $70.6 (+1.81%) off Monday's $3,898.9 print and back above the $3,900 put wall it had been sitting on. ATM IV cooled to 22.29% from 23.67% (-1.38pp), trimming the 1σ daily move to $55.70 (1.40%). The put wall snapped back from $3,900 to $3,500 (6,003 contracts) as Monday's spot-level hedges decayed, restoring a $470 structural cushion beneath price. Put volume collapsed to 3,913 against 5,849 calls (0.67x) after Monday's 1.77x panic-hedging spike — the downside bid has gone quiet.
five_day_thesis: Five sessions ago spot was $4,074.5 with ATM IV at 20.12% and dealers net long gamma (+27.03 in the ±20% band); price is now $105.0 lower (-2.58%) and dealers have been short gamma for three consecutive sessions. The important change this session is that the short-gamma extreme is unwinding, not deepening: window net GEX improved from -314.27 to -92.31 (a 71% reduction) and the gamma flip strike lifted $3,120 → $3,180, both consistent with Monday's panic puts bleeding out rather than new downside structure being built. Inside ±$200 of spot the book is still firmly short gamma at -308.6 (puts -513.0 against calls +204.4), so the tradeable range remains vol-amplifying even as the tail hedges decay. Call OI grew +17,704 over the window versus +8,552 puts, holding P/C OI pinned at 0.40 and leaving every meaningful resistance wall far overhead — $4,500 (11,031), $4,725 (9,542), $4,800 (8,635). Max pain has bled $5,400 → $5,250 (-$150) while spot fell, keeping the gap at +$1,280 (+32.3%): that figure is legacy high-strike OI, not a magnet, and should be ignored for positioning.
what_changed: Net GEX (±20% band) improved -314.27 → -92.31 — short gamma down 71% in one session, the first contraction after two sessions of expansion
Put wall reverted $3,900 → $3,500 (6,003 OI) — Monday's at-the-money hedges decayed, restoring a $470 cushion below spot
ATM IV compressed 23.67% → 22.29% (-1.38pp) — 1σ daily narrows to $55.70 from $58.14, though still +2.17pp over the 5-day window
Put/call volume flipped 1.77 → 0.67 — 3,913 puts vs 5,849 calls, downside demand exhausted after Monday's 11,916-put spike
Gamma flip strike lifted $3,120 → $3,180 — floor of the short-gamma corridor rising with price
Max pain drifted $5,400 → $5,250 (-$150) across the window while spot fell $105.0 — gap now +$1,280, a legacy-OI artifact
prediction: Bias constructive above $3,950 while the short-gamma unwind continues: the path of least resistance is a grind toward the $4,050 call shelf (1,810 OI) and then $4,100 (3,544 OI), the first strike in the near field with positive net gamma (+17.1). The thesis breaks below $3,950, where put gamma of -50.5 reactivates the amplification mechanics and opens a retest of the $3,900 wall (5,825 put OI). With net GEX at -308.6 inside ±$200, expect range expansion on any break of either edge — moves will overshoot rather than fade.
